title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks fell for a 4th straight session Thursday (S&P 500 -0.5% to 7,636.36, Dow -405 pts/-0.8% to 52,380.66, Nasdaq -0.6% to 26,253.34) as hot inflation data and surging oil weighed on sentiment.
Markets: Brent crude jumped 6.3% to $107.63/barrel, its highest since the Iran war escalated, after Houthi attacks wounded 73 people at Saudi energy facilities and halted some operations.
Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 4.95%, a fresh ~3-year high, as the bond selloff continued despite the Fed's ongoing buyback operation; the dollar hit a one-week high.
Companies: Nvidia invested roughly $3.5B into a Qualcomm-rival AI chip effort, pushing further into the AI stack; chip and AI-related stocks broadly slid Thursday in the risk-off mood.
Companies: Kroger reports earnings today, offering a read on consumer spending as energy and food costs climb.

Macro/Policy: August PPI ran hot Thursday: headline +0.4% M/M as expected but +5.4% Y/Y (above forecast) on surging energy costs (diesel +24%); core PPI +0.2% M/M, +4.6% Y/Y, pushing Fed rate-hike odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting to roughly 70%.
Macro/Policy: August CPI is due today at 8:30am ET, with consensus near 3.3-3.4% headline Y/Y and ~2.4% core Y/Y — a pivotal print ahead of next week's Fed decision.
Macro/Policy: Existing home sales fell, adding to signs of a cooling economy even as inflation pressures build.
